note.question: How do cloud providers' and users' joint security investments, cloud usage, provider competition, and switching costs shape the long-run paths of cloud security, vulnerability, lock-in, and user welfare?
note.overview: The paper is an infinite-horizon dynamic game between two competing cloud service providers and their users. Providers and users sequentially invest in security and users choose cloud usage conditional on Markov states; the paper characterizes a symmetric stationary Markov-perfect equilibrium with no-switching constraints.

components.label: Symmetric stationary Markov-perfect equilibrium with CSP no-switching constraints
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Symmetric stationary Markov-perfect equilibrium with CSP no-switching constraints. Section 3.6 defines stationary Markov strategies and requires subgame perfection in every state. Sections 4-5 derive user value functions and equilibrium paths, impose no-switching and participation constraints, and characterize the competing CSPs' security responses.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: In each period t, each CSP first chooses security investment s_csp,j,t. Given the provider's investment, its users choose their own security investments s_i,t. Users then choose cloud-service usage y_i,t under the resulting security umbrella; stay/switch choices must satisfy no-switching and participation constraints. Accumulated security S_j,t and vulnerability V_j,t become the next period's Markov states. providers move before their own users within each period security effort and usage jointly determine next-period vulnerability
